questions.question: Which large Harappan settlement situated in Haryana is recognized as one of the largest sites of the Indus civilization?
questions.explanation: Rakhigarhi in Hisar district, Haryana, spans over 350 hectares, making it one of the largest Harappan sites.

questions.question: In the craft production of Harappan stone beads, tiny perforations were made using specialized drills made of chert or bronze discovered at:
options: B) Harappa and Kot Diji only
questions.explanation: Specialized micro-drills for perforating stone beads have been recovered from Chanhudaro, Lothal, and Dholavira.

questions.question: What archaeological evidence from Harappan domestic houses suggests that many dwellings were two storeys high?
options: A) Burnt brick staircases leading to an upper floor or flat roof
D) Surviving wooden balconies preserved in ice
questions.explanation: Remains of brick stairways ascending from courtyards show that numerous Harappan houses had a second storey or rooftop living areas.

questions.question: In his report on the decline of Harappa, who proposed the dramatic hypothesis of an "Aryan massacre" at Mohenjodaro, later debunked by modern forensic research?
questions.explanation: Mortimer Wheeler cited unburied skeletons in Mohenjodaro streets and Rigvedic verses mentioning Indra as 'Purandara' to argue for an Aryan onslaught, a theory later discredited.

questions.sub_topic: Political and Economic Systems in Early States
questions.question: In the Mauryan administrative system, the imperial revenue assessor and chief tax collector was designated as the:
questions.explanation: According to the Arthashastra, the Samaharta was the royal collector-general responsible for assessing and collecting imperial revenues.

questions.sub_topic: Political and Economic Systems in Early States
questions.question: Which ancient Indian dynasty of northern India was celebrated for its high-purity gold coinage depicting kings playing the veena or performing the Ashvamedha sacrifice?
questions.explanation: Gupta monarchs issued artistic gold coins (dinaras) depicting Samudragupta playing the lyre (veena) and performing Vedic horse sacrifices.

questions.sub_topic: Political and Economic Systems in Early States
questions.question: In the Prayaga Prashasti of Samudragupta, which distinct imperial policy was adopted toward the twelve defeated rulers of Dakshinapatha (southern India)?
options: A) Grahana-Mokshanugraha (capturing them, releasing them, and reinstating them as tributary vassals)
B) Complete physical extermination and annexation of their territories
C) Forcible deportation of their royal families to Central Asia
D) Imposition of compulsory Buddhist monastic vows on their courts
questions.explanation: Harishena recorded that Samudragupta captured and then liberated the kings of Dakshinapatha, allowing them to rule on payment of regular tribute.

questions.sub_topic: Political and Economic Systems in Early States
questions.question: The Eran stone pillar inscription of Bhanugupta in Madhya Pradesh (510 CE) is historically noteworthy because it contains the earliest inscriptional reference to:
options: A) The practice of Sati (widow immolation following her husband Goparaja's death in battle)
B) The construction of an underground canal on the Narmada
C) A royal land tax reduction following crop failure
D) The appointment of a Greek general to command royal elephants
questions.explanation: The Eran inscription of 510 CE records that the wife of general Goparaja accompanied him onto the funeral pyre after he fell in battle against the Hunas.

questions.question: In ancient Brahmanical society, the social mechanism created to assign individuals to groups based on birth and occupation was:
questions.explanation: Jati was an occupational, kinship-based category into which individuals were born, functioning as the practical organizing framework within the four varnas.

questions.question: In the legal norms of the Dharmashastras, what was the "Anuloma" form of marriage?
options: A) A marriage between a man of a higher varna and a woman of a lower varna
B) A marriage between a woman of a higher varna and a man of a lower varna
C) A marriage between partners of the same gotra
D) A marriage where the bride chose her husband through public combat
questions.explanation: Anuloma was a union where the male partner belonged to a higher varna than the female; the reverse (Pratiloma) was condemned by orthodoxy.

questions.question: When the Chinese pilgrim Xuan Zang visited India in the seventh century CE, he observed that executioners, scavengers, and outcasts were legally required to:
options: A) Live outside the boundary walls of towns and enter only when summoned
B) Wear distinctive yellow silk turbans
C) Pay a special head-tax to Buddhist monasteries
D) Speak exclusively in classical Sanskrit
questions.explanation: Xuan Zang noted that butchers, executioners, and scavengers were forced to dwell outside city limits and their houses were marked with distinctive signs.

questions.question: In the Buddhist Sutta Pitaka (Agganna Sutta), how is the origin of kingship and social hierarchy explained as an alternative to the divine creation story of the Purusha Sukta?
options: A) Through a social contract where humans elected a charismatic leader called the "Mahasammata" (the Great Chosen One) to maintain order in exchange for a share of rice
B) Through a military coup executed by foreign mercenaries
C) Through an absolute decree handed down by Brahma on a golden leaf
D) Through the miraculous emergence of an armed emperor from a volcanic lake
questions.explanation: The Agganna Sutta offers a rationalist social contract myth: people chose the Mahasammata to enforce justice and prevent theft, agreeing to pay him a fraction of their harvest.

questions.question: Which of the following forms the core ethical foundation of the Jain path to liberation (Triratna)?
options: A) Right Empire, Right War, and Right Conquest
B) Right Faith, Right Knowledge, and Right Conduct
C) Right Wealth, Right Commerce, and Right Profit
D) Right Ritual, Right Sacrifice, and Right Mantra
questions.explanation: The Three Jewels (Triratna) of Jainism are Samyak Darshana (Right Faith), Samyak Jnana (Right Knowledge), and Samyak Charitra (Right Conduct).

questions.question: In Buddhist philosophy, the doctrine of "Anicca" (impermanence) teaches that:
options: A) The physical world was created in six calendar days by a divine architect
B) The phenomenal world is transient, in constant flux, and devoid of any permanent enduring soul
C) Every human action is pre-determined by immutable astrology
D) Material wealth multiplies automatically through ascetic chants
questions.explanation: Buddhism views the world as anicca (transient/impermanent) and anatta (soulless); sorrow arises from attachment to that which is constantly changing.

questions.question: Why did H.H. Cole, the Superintendent of Architectural Monuments, advocate in 1880 that ancient Indian architectural masterworks like Sanchi should be preserved in situ?
options: A) He believed the stone carvings carried toxic subterranean radiation
B) He argued it was a suicidal vandalism to strip original monuments of their parts to deposit them in distant foreign museums
C) He lacked funds to hire maritime transport ships
D) Queen Victoria ordered all Indian stones to remain uncatalogued
questions.explanation: Major Cole argued that European museums should be satisfied with plaster casts, maintaining that stripping original monuments was an act of cultural plunder.

questions.question: In early Buddhist canonical texts, the monastic order of nuns (bhikkhunis) were required to observe eight strict rules of subordination to the monks, known as the:
questions.explanation: The Garudhammas (Eight Heavy Rules) were structural conditions under which the Buddha allowed the establishment of the Bhikkhuni Sangha.

questions.question: Which prominent Italian traveler visited India in the late 13th century and left accounts of southern maritime coastal trade?
questions.explanation: The Venetian merchant Marco Polo traveled through southern Indian coastal ports (including the Pandyan realm) on his voyage from China around 1292 CE.

questions.question: Al-Biruni documented that beyond the four classical varnas, there existed eight occupational groups called "Antyaja", which included:
options: A) High state finance ministers and cavalry commanders
B) Fullers, shoemakers, weavers, jugglers, fishermen, and hunters
C) Sanskrit astrologers and ayurvedic physicians
questions.explanation: Al-Biruni described the Antyaja as eight craft groups who rendered services but were segregated below the four varnas, marrying only among themselves.

questions.question: In his graphic accounts of medieval Indian social practices, which distressing scene at Lahore did Francois Bernier witness and describe with intense horror?
options: A) A gladiatorial combat between two war elephants in the public street
B) The forced self-immolation (Sati) of an emotionally terrified twelve-year-old child widow
C) The public execution of a European Jesuit priest by imperial archers
D) A naval battle between French and Portuguese galleys on the Ravi river
questions.explanation: Bernier wrote of his profound shock upon witnessing the tragic burning of an unwilling twelve-year-old widow who was tied to the funeral pyre by relatives.

questions.question: The French political philosopher Montesquieu used Francois Bernier's travel accounts to construct which theoretical concept regarding Asian state systems?
questions.explanation: Montesquieu argued that Asian rulers possessed despotic power over all subjects because the absolute monarch claimed sole ownership over all land.

questions.question: The four foundational Nayanar saint-poets of Tamil Nadu whose devotional hymns are enshrined in the Tevaram are:
options: A) Nammalvar, Madhurakavi, Andal, and Kulasekhara
B) Appar, Sambandar, Sundarar, and Manikkavachakar
C) Basavanna, Allama Prabhu, Channabasavanna, and Siddharama
D) Kabir, Nanak, Ravidas, and Namdev
questions.explanation: The four great Shaiva teachers of Tamil Nadu celebrated in the Tevaram and Tirumurai are Appar, Sambandar, Sundarar, and Manikkavachakar.

questions.question: In North Indian vernacular Bhakti, the enigmatic poems of Kabir that use paradoxical, inverted symbolism are known as:
questions.explanation: Kabir composed ulatbansi poems where normal meanings are overturned (e.g. "the lotus blossoms without water", "the ocean burns in fire") to express transcendent truth.

questions.question: Why did the Virashaiva (Lingayat) community in 12th-century Karnataka diverge radically from orthodox Brahmanical funerary practices?
options: A) They cast ashes into the Arabian Sea exclusively
B) They buried their dead instead of cremating them, believing that the departed soul united directly with Shiva and would not be reborn
C) They preserved bodies inside limestone sarcophagi
D) They performed human sacrifices at cremation grounds
questions.explanation: Lingayats do not cremate their dead or observe post-cremation pollution rites; they bury their dead, believing devotees merge eternally with Shiva upon death.

questions.question: Who was the renowned court poet, musician, and devoted disciple of Shaikh Nizamuddin Auliya credited with developing the qawwali form of Sufi music?
questions.explanation: Amir Khusrau was the musical genius who blended Persian and Indian styles, composing the qaul (saying) that gave qawwali its liturgical and artistic form.

questions.sub_topic: Vijayanagara Empire: Politics, Economy and Architecture
questions.question: The suburban township founded by Krishnadeva Raya near the capital of Vijayanagara was named Nagalapuram in honor of his:
questions.explanation: Krishnadeva Raya built the suburban township of Nagalapuram near Vijayanagara and named it in filial devotion after his mother Nagala Devi.

questions.sub_topic: Vijayanagara Empire: Politics, Economy and Architecture
questions.question: In the Vitthala temple complex at Hampi, which musical architectural feature astonishes visitors?
options: A) Water pipes hidden in the floor that play flute melodies
B) Automatic bronze bells powered by steam pumps
C) The monolithic musical stone pillars that produce resonant acoustic notes when tapped
D) Wooden beams carved with acoustic resonance boxes
questions.explanation: The Ranga Mandapa of the Vitthala temple contains 56 musical stone pillars carved from granite that resonate with tonal frequencies when gently struck.

questions.sub_topic: Vijayanagara Empire: Politics, Economy and Architecture
questions.question: Following the cataclysmic Battle of Talikota (1565), which surviving dynasty ruled the remnants of the Vijayanagara Empire from Penukonda and Chandragiri?
questions.explanation: Tirumala Raya shifted the imperial court southward to Penukonda and later Chandragiri, inaugurating the rule of the fourth dynasty, the Aravidu.

questions.sub_topic: Vijayanagara Empire: Politics, Economy and Architecture
questions.question: In his account of Vijayanagara fortifications, how did Abdur Razzaq describe the method of joining the massive masonry stone blocks without mortar?
options: A) The blocks were glued with resin extracted from banyan trees
B) The stones were joined with molten copper and lead poured into iron rivets
C) The stones were wedge-shaped and held together without any mortar or cementing agent, fitting seamlessly together by precise carving
D) The walls were made of sun-dried mud bricks coated with white plaster
questions.explanation: Abdur Razzaq marveled that the stone fortress blocks were cut wedge-shaped and fitted without lime or mortar, yet possessed impregnable strength.

questions.sub_topic: The Mughal Empire and Agrarian Society
questions.question: In Mughal India, which silver coin weighing approximately 178 grains became the standard currency of commercial transactions throughout the subcontinent?
questions.explanation: Introduced originally by Sher Shah Suri and refined under Akbar, the silver Rupiya served as the universally accepted standard currency of the empire.

questions.sub_topic: The Mughal Empire and Agrarian Society
questions.question: In the land survey system formulated under Raja Todar Mal, the measuring rod made of bamboo sticks linked with iron rings was termed the:
questions.explanation: Akbar replaced the earlier measuring rope (which expanded in humidity and shrank in heat) with the tanab, a bamboo rod joined by iron rings.

questions.sub_topic: The Mughal Empire and Agrarian Society
questions.question: In rural Maharashtra of the 17th century, village artisans and hereditary functionaries were entitled to a fixed customary share of grain known as the:
questions.explanation: The balutedari system guaranteed village artisans (balutedars) customary agricultural produce (baluta) in exchange for their continuous professional services.

questions.sub_topic: The Mughal Empire and Agrarian Society
questions.question: Why did the influx of American silver bullion (via European trade) into Mughal India in the 16th and 17th centuries not cause runaway hyperinflation?
options: A) Foreign traders were forbidden from using coins inside India
B) The emperor ordered all silver bullion to be buried in the Himalayas
C) It was absorbed by massive coin minting, commercial monetization, and economic expansion across rural and urban markets
D) Silver was converted immediately into lead ammunition
questions.explanation: The expanding monetization of agricultural taxes, vibrant handicraft production, and trade allowed the economy to absorb silver smoothly, stabilizing prices.

questions.question: The Santhals referred to outside moneylenders, traders, and British colonial officials who exploited them in the Rajmahal hills by the derogatory term:
questions.explanation: The Santhals termed corrupt outside moneylenders, grain dealers, and Company tax agents "Dikus" (literally outsiders/exploiters).

questions.question: What legal strategy did Bengal zamindars adopt to evade the loss of their lands during colonial revenue auctions?
options: A) Demolishing all ancestral buildings and temples
B) Surrendering their estates to foreign American banks
C) Transferring titles to female relatives (such as mothers), whose property could not be legally confiscated under Company law
D) Submitting forged letters claiming the land belonged to the Mughal emperor
questions.explanation: Zamindars transferred properties to their mothers or wives, because British regulations forbade the seizure and auction of women's estates.

questions.question: The Deccan Agriculturists' Relief Act was enacted by the British colonial administration in which year to protect indebted peasants from moneylenders?
questions.explanation: Following the Deccan Riots Commission report, the government passed the Deccan Agriculturists' Relief Act of 1879 to prevent the arrest and land alienation of indebted ryots.

questions.question: Why did the British collector of Bhagalpur, Augustus Cleveland, adopt a policy of pacification with the Paharia chiefs in the 1780s?
options: A) He cleared all Rajmahal forests to construct military airports
B) He forced all Paharia children into British boarding schools
C) He offered tribal chiefs annual stipends in exchange for ensuring orderly conduct and monitoring their clansmen
D) He relocated all Paharias to coastal Bengal
questions.explanation: Cleveland gave annual stipends to Paharia sardars, making them responsible for the discipline of their men in return for tribal peace.

questions.question: Which prominent taluqdar fort in Awadh held out heroically against British artillery attacks for months during the 1857 rebellion?
options: C) The fort of Raja Beni Madho of Shankarpur
D) The Red Fort of Agra
questions.explanation: Raja Beni Madho of Shankarpur was an Awadh taluqdar who led thousands of armed retainers, resisting British columns long after the fall of Lucknow.

questions.question: Who was the Chief Commissioner of Awadh who fortified the British Residency at Lucknow and died of wounds during the rebel siege in July 1857?
questions.explanation: Sir Henry Lawrence prepared the Lucknow Residency for siege but was mortally wounded by an artillery shell on 2 July 1857, dying two days later.

questions.question: In the tribal plateau of Singhbhum in Chota Nagpur, which local tribal leader mobilized the Kol and Ho tribes to fight British colonial forces during 1857?
questions.explanation: Gonoo, a cultivated Kol rebel cultivator of Singhbhum, mobilized tribal fighters and fought alongside Raja Arjun Singh of Porahat during 1857.

questions.question: The British commander who recaptured Delhi in September 1857 through brutal street fighting and was mortally wounded at the Kashmir Gate was:
questions.explanation: Brigadier-General John Nicholson led the desperate assault on the Kashmir Gate in Delhi on 14 September 1857, dying of gunshot wounds nine days later.

questions.question: In 1930, while Mahatma Gandhi marched to Dandi, which nationalist leader led a parallel salt satyagraha march from Tiruchirappalli to Vedaranyam in Tamil Nadu?
questions.explanation: C. Rajagopalachari (Rajaji) organized and led the historic Vedaranyam Salt March along the Tanjore coast in April 1930.

questions.question: In the Northwest Frontier Province, who organized the non-violent volunteer movement of Pashtuns known as the Khudai Khidmatgars (Red Shirts)?
options: D) Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan (Frontier Gandhi)
questions.explanation: Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan founded the Khudai Khidmatgars, dedicating thousands of Pathans to absolute non-violent satyagraha against British rule.

questions.question: In 1942, the British government dispatched Sir Stafford Cripps to India with a draft declaration offering Dominion Status primarily because:
options: A) The League of Nations ordered an immediate plebiscite
B) The British Treasury had run out of silver to pay civil servants in Delhi
C) American President Roosevelt threatened to annex British India
D) The Japanese military had captured Burma, threatened an invasion of India, and the British needed Indian political cooperation for the war effort
questions.explanation: With Japanese troops sweeping through Malaya and Burma to the borders of Assam in 1942, Churchill's war cabinet sent Cripps to secure Indian support.

questions.question: Who was the 73-year-old heroic woman revolutionary who led a procession to hoist the national flag at the Tamluk police station in Midnapore in 1942 and was shot dead by police?
questions.explanation: Matangini Hazra, lovingly called "Gandhi Buri", led 6,000 protesters during Quit India and kept holding the tricolor aloft even after being shot multiple times.

questions.question: In the Constituent Assembly, who served as the Minister for Food and Agriculture and chaired the Union Constitution Committee?
questions.explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru chaired key committees including the Union Constitution Committee and the States Committee.

questions.question: In the Constituent Assembly debates on citizenship, which member from the United Provinces, Begum Aizaz Rasul, argued strongly that:
options: A) The British Crown should appoint the Governor-General permanently
B) All women should be barred from contesting parliamentary elections
C) Urdu should be the sole language of the supreme court
D) Separate electorates were self-destructive and isolated the Muslim minority from the national mainstream
questions.explanation: Begum Aizaz Rasul, the only Muslim woman in the Constituent Assembly, courageously denounced separate electorates as detrimental to minority integration.

questions.question: During the language controversies, which prominent woman member from the Madras Presidency, G. Durgabai, warned the Assembly that:
options: A) Sanskrit was the only language capable of being written in modern law
B) English should be made compulsory in all primary schools forever
C) Telugu should replace Sanskrit in all religious ceremonies
D) The aggressive propaganda for Hindi in the South was creating deep hostility and alienating millions of peaceful non-Hindi speakers
questions.explanation: G. Durgabai pointed out that non-Hindi citizens who had embraced Hindi voluntarily felt aggrieved by the aggressive zeal with which Hindi proponents tried to impose it.

questions.question: In the final speech delivered by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar to the Constituent Assembly on 25 November 1949, he warned that political democracy would remain fragile unless accompanied by:
options: A) Permanent judicial control over all industrial factories
B) Compulsory military service for all university graduates
C) A massive expansion of the police force in every village
D) Social and economic democracy, eliminating the contradiction of "one man, one vote" alongside deep social inequality
questions.explanation: Ambedkar warned: "We are going to enter into a life of contradictions. In politics we will have equality and in social and economic life we will have inequality..."

questions.sub_topic: Political and Economic Systems in Early States
questions.question: Which ancient Tamil Sangam anthology contains vivid descriptions of the affluent coastal emporium of Puhar (Kaveripattinam) and its bustling international docks?
questions.explanation: Pattinappalai in the Sangam corpus provides detailed portrayals of the goods entering Puhar—horses from Arabia, gems from Sri Lanka, and sandalwood from the Western Ghats.

questions.question: During the horrific communal riots following Partition in 1946-1947, Mahatma Gandhi traveled on foot through which violence-torn district of East Bengal to restore peace?
questions.explanation: Gandhiji walked barefoot through the villages of Noakhali in eastern Bengal, staying in rural huts to protect minorities and quell communal violence.
